newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels advance on several fronts.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels advance on several fronts.

text.p: Zaire's rebels, whose deadline for the army to lay down its arms expired on Thursday, are apparently advancing on several fronts -- notably in or near the economically vital mineral provinces of Shaba and Kasai.
The Zairean Defence Ministry and rebel radio in the east reported rebel movements in Shaba and near Kasai, with the government sending reinforcements to Kasai's capital.
But the ministry said on Thursday that the strategic town of Kisangani, the army's headquarters in the war zone and a prime target of the rebels, was quiet.

On the diplomatic front, France called for a "security framework" for Zaire -- code words for a multinational force. Kenya downgraded a planned March 19 mini summit on Zaire to a preparatory meeting for a full regional summit later.
Zaire's defence ministry said government naval units clashed on Wednesday with rebels advancing south in dug-out canoes on Lake Tanganyika in Shaba.

"Elements of the naval force intercepted the enemy boats. In the clashes that ensued 11 rebels were killed and eight captured including one woman," the spokesman said, adding rebels used canoes to seize Kalemie and Moba ports to the north.
The spokesman said the rebels were advancing towards the port of Moliro around 160 km (100 miles) south of Moba which they captured on Sunday.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.

The ministry has also reported reinforcements being sent to defend the capital of the diamond-rich Kasai. "We have sent reinforcements to Mbuji Mayi as a precaution against any attacks by the enemy there," the spokesman said earlier.
Shaba and Kasai and copper, diamonds or other minerals mined there are at the heart of Zaire's economy and state revenues.
The rebels gave government forces until today Thursday to lay down their arms or face an all-out assault on Kisangani.

Military analysts say that the combined forces of the notoriously ill-disciplined Zairean army's better troops, Serb mercenaries and allied Rwandan Hutu hardliners might slow a rebel advance on the city.
The army, which has helicopter gunships, has sown minefields around the city.
To the south of Kisangani, tired and frightened Rwandan Hutu refugees limped into the town of Ubundu on the Zaire River accusing the world of abandoning them.
U.N. refugee officials told visiting journalists about 75,000 refugees had reached Ubundu. Most fled Rwanda fearing reprisals in 1994 after the genocide by Hutu hardliners of minority Tutsis.
Refugees spoke of passing dead and dying refugees on the way from Tingi Tingi camp about 150 km (90 miles) to the east.
In Geneva, the U.N. said its special human rights investigator would visit Zaire to probe allegations of massacres of Hutu refugees by rebels.

Earlier, state radio accused Angola of recruiting and training its own fighters to join the rebels. "These are reinforcements that (rebel leader) Laurent Kabila is waiting for before attacking Kisangani, which is too difficult for the rebels (to take) alone," it said.

Zaire accuses neighbours Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of invading in support of the rebels, who vow to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko. Mobutu had cancer surgery in Europe last August and has spent most of his time there since then.
